teams.appointed: Announced by the DFB on 24 July 2026 (four-year contract to 2030). He took over from Nagelsmann on 15 August 2026.
teams.replaced_reason: Nagelsmann stepped down after Germany lost to Paraguay in the 2026 World Cup round of 32, the nation's first World Cup penalty-shootout defeat.

institution_quote.quote: he can develop young players and get his teams to perform under pressure
institution_quote.speaker: Rudi Völler, DFB sporting director (partial quote of his statement on the appointment)
institution_quote.source: DFB (German Football Association), 'Jürgen Klopp appointed new Germany head coach'

coach_promise.quote: I want people to go home thinking ‘Wow, that was cool!’
coach_promise.source: FIFA.com, quoting Klopp at his unveiling in Frankfurt, 24 July 2026

key_choices.text: For his first four Nations League games Klopp named 44 players, including 16 uncapped, and split them into two squads.
Joshua Kimmich kept the captain's armband under Klopp.
Klopp named Marc-André ter Stegen as Germany's number one goalkeeper 'for the moment'.
His first squad left out Deniz Undav, Leroy Sané and Oliver Baumann.

For the November window he cut the group to 24 and recalled Niclas Füllkrug. He also gave a first senior call-up to Wael Mohya and kept five recent debutants, including Jonas Urbig, Said El Mala and Philipp Treu.
At his unveiling Klopp said Germany would play with four defenders and rely on wingers, and that some players would get opportunities they did not expect.
Against the Netherlands Klopp started Ter Stegen; Treu, Schlotterbeck, Tah, Brown; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Gruda, Wirtz, Scherhant; Havertz.

links.text: Klopp's first match as Germany coach was against the Netherlands, then coached by another new man, Xavi. It ended 1-1 in Amsterdam, with Völler asking for patience.

Before the World Cup opener against Curaçao, Klopp, working as a TV pundit, said 'luckily Julian Nagelsmann picks the team – for now'. He later apologised on air, and a few weeks later he was named Nagelsmann's successor.
Germany lost 0-1 to Greece in Klopp's first home game, a defeat described as historic.
The 5-0 win over the Netherlands on 16 November 2026 sealed Germany's place in the Nations League quarter-finals. Al Jazeera called it the Dutch side's heaviest defeat in 67 years.

teams.appointed: Announced by the KNVB on 12 August 2026 (contract to the 2030 World Cup). He was presented in Zeist on 25 August 2026.
teams.replaced_reason: Koeman resigned on 30 June 2026, hours after the Netherlands lost on penalties to Morocco in the World Cup round of 32. He said the responsibility ultimately rests with the head coach.

institution_quote.quote: a footballing vision that aligns very well with the way we want the Netherlands national team to play
institution_quote.speaker: Nigel de Jong, KNVB Director of Elite Football (partial quote)
